discovery: Development of next-generation DNA sequencing (massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis using reversible terminator chemistry and clonal cluster amplification)
rationale: The 2025 prize (MOFs) went to materials chemistry, and the committee often alternates toward the chemistry–biology interface. Next-generation sequencing is a chemistry-driven invention that has transformed biology and medicine, and it has the kind of broad impact the committee tends to reward. Its inventors have already received major precursor awards: the Millennium Technology Prize (2020) and the Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences (2022). The field is also mature and the inventors are clearly identified, which makes it a top-tier candidate. Controlled radical polymerization (Matyjaszewski, Sawamoto) and nanomedicine/drug delivery (Langer, Maeda, Matsumura) are the main alternatives.
